unchanged_record_reason: Source-reviewed v2 wording encodes byte-identically to the accepted canonical SC0 record.

records.english: Where did Julio go?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: At the start of Julio's market tutorial, Raphael looks around after losing sight of him.
records.source_meaning: Raphael wonders where Julio has gone.
records.localization_note: Condensed the two Japanese questions into one natural spoken question.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Over here!{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio calls to Raphael from the market.
records.source_meaning: Julio calls out that he is over here.
records.localization_note: Removed the repeated deictic phrase while retaining Julio's loud call.

records.english: The Market...{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael realizes Julio has led him to the market.
records.source_meaning: Raphael recognizes that this is the market.
records.localization_note: Market follows the project's established interface term.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Start by selling some trade goods here. You can sell anything we bought in Lisbon. But remember...{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio begins the market tutorial by having Raphael sell the cargo purchased in Lisbon.
records.source_meaning: Julio tells Raphael to begin by selling trade goods here, including anything bought in Lisbon, then introduces a caveat.
records.localization_note: Recast Julio's elderly sentence endings as clear tutorial speech without flattening his mentor voice.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}You need a contract to sell goods.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains the requirement that limits trade in a city.
records.source_meaning: Julio says a contract is required before goods can be sold.
records.localization_note: States the rule directly in natural tutorial language.

records.english: A contract?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks Julio to explain the unfamiliar trade requirement.
records.source_meaning: Raphael repeats contract as a surprised question.
records.localization_note: The concise question is idiomatic and faithful.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Pay at the Palace or Governor's Office to earn local trade rights.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains where and how Raphael obtains a trade contract.
records.source_meaning: Julio says to visit the palace or governor's office, pay a contract fee to the ruler, and receive the right to trade.
records.localization_note: Uses established location and trading-right terminology and divides the procedure into two clear sentences.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Make contracts in many cities. Pay the minimum at first.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio advises Raphael on an economical early-game contracting strategy.
records.source_meaning: Julio recommends contracting in many cities and says the minimum contract payment is enough at first.
records.localization_note: Turned the Japanese reassurance into concise strategic advice.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}The Ceuta contract is settled. Next city's up to you.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio tells Raphael that the tutorial has prearranged Ceuta's contract but future contracts are his responsibility.
records.source_meaning: Julio says he made the Ceuta contract and Raphael must handle contracts from the next city onward.
records.localization_note: Makes the handoff of responsibility explicit without adding information.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Have goods to sell? Sell them now.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio prompts Raphael to complete the market transaction.
records.source_meaning: Julio tells Raphael to sell any goods he wants to sell.
records.localization_note: Rendered the emphatic command as a direct tutorial prompt.

records.english: All right.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael agrees to sell the goods as Julio instructed.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says yes and that he will do so.
records.localization_note: A concise, natural acknowledgment preserves Raphael's ready agreement without using the renderer-unsafe uppercase ASCII I.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Whew. Hayreddin saved our lives.{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: After surviving a pirate encounter, Claudio credits Hayreddin with their escape.
records.source_meaning: Claudio sighs in relief and says they survived thanks to Hayreddin.
records.localization_note: Saved our lives naturally conveys the Japanese idiom for narrowly escaping death.

records.english: Mm...{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael quietly agrees with Claudio after the dangerous encounter.
records.source_meaning: Raphael gives a subdued agreement.
records.localization_note: Yeah preserves the subdued, informal response.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}At this rate, an enemy fleet may challenge us sooner than we expect.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio uses the recent danger to introduce advanced sailing actions and combat preparation.
records.source_meaning: Julio warns that an enemy fleet may pick a fight with them surprisingly soon.
records.localization_note: Challenge us is natural and preserves the possibility of an enemy-initiated battle.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Let's cover your other sea options.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio offers the next sailing tutorial after warning about enemy fleets.
records.source_meaning: Julio says he should teach Raphael the other actions available at sea.
records.localization_note: Uses a direct mentor voice appropriate to the tutorial choice that follows.

records.english: Please do.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael accepts Julio's offer to explain the sailing actions.
records.source_meaning: Raphael politely asks Julio to proceed.
records.localization_note: Please do is concise, polite, and fits the binary tutorial choice.

records.english: No, thanks.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael declines Julio's optional explanation.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says he will be fine without further help.
records.localization_note: No, thanks is the natural American response for declining optional instruction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Let's cover three actions: inspect, battle, and search.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio introduces the three sailing actions covered by the tutorial.
records.source_meaning: Julio says he will explain looking around at sea, initiating combat, and searching.
records.localization_note: Uses parallel imperative verbs and the established action names for a readable tutorial list.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}To inspect a nearby city or fleet, or to attack one, you must first select it as your target.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains the shared targeting step for inspection and battle.
records.source_meaning: Julio says a nearby city or fleet must be selected when viewing detailed information or initiating a battle.
records.localization_note: Reordered the conditional Japanese sentence into a clear player action and requirement.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Search along the coast. You may uncover quite a lot.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains where the search action is most useful.
records.source_meaning: Julio says searching near coastlines can uncover various things.
records.localization_note: Converted the tentative Japanese phrasing into natural tutorial advice while retaining may.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Well? Got it?{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio checks Raphael's understanding after the sailing tutorial panels.
records.source_meaning: Julio asks whether Raphael understands.
records.localization_note: The clipped questions match Julio's practical teaching style.

records.english: Yes. Thank you, Julio.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael confirms that he understands and thanks Julio for the lesson.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says yes and thanks Julio politely.
records.localization_note: Added Julio's name to make the formal Japanese thanks sound natural in English without changing the addressee.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Good. Stay alert at sea.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio closes the lesson with a warning about the dangers of sailing.
records.source_meaning: Julio acknowledges Raphael and warns him never to become careless at sea.
records.localization_note: Let your guard down is the direct idiomatic equivalent of the Japanese warning.

records.english: Yes.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael accepts Julio's warning.
records.source_meaning: Raphael answers affirmatively.
records.localization_note: Right sounds more natural than a formal yes in this mentor-student exchange.

records.english: (Someday, surely...){PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael privately renews his determination after Julio's tutorial and warning.
records.source_meaning: Raphael thinks that someday, surely, his hope will come true; the object is deliberately unstated in this fragment.
records.localization_note: Retains the source's unresolved inward thought instead of inventing its object.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Hayreddin's intent is unclear, but the Mediterranean should be safer.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: After Hayreddin's intervention, Julio assesses what it means for their Mediterranean travel.
records.source_meaning: Julio cannot yet understand Hayreddin's true intentions, but thinks Mediterranean passage should now be manageable.
records.localization_note: Safer now naturally expresses the practical effect without claiming the sea is completely safe.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}True. We won't last long if pirates attack every time we enter.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus agrees with Julio that repeated pirate attacks would make Mediterranean travel untenable.
records.source_meaning: Janus says that being attacked by such pirates every time they enter the Mediterranean would cost more lives than they have.
records.localization_note: We wouldn't last long localizes the exaggerated life-count idiom without weakening the danger.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Still, avoid the Ottomans; they're too dangerous.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio identifies the Ottoman-controlled waters as the next major strategic danger.
records.source_meaning: Julio says they cannot approach the Ottoman Empire because the risk is too great.
records.localization_note: Uses Ottoman Empire rather than a literal hybrid country name for idiomatic historical English.

records.english: Why is that?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks Julio why Ottoman waters are so dangerous.
records.source_meaning: Raphael asks for the reason.
records.localization_note: The direct question is natural and preserves Raphael's polite curiosity.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Eastern Mediterranean waters belong to the Ottoman Pasha. We wouldn't stand a chance against his fleet.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains the political and military reason for avoiding eastern Mediterranean waters.
records.source_meaning: Julio says roughly the eastern half of the Mediterranean belongs to the Ottoman Turks and the Pasha's forces, whom they could not defeat if attacked.
records.localization_note: Combines the overlapping Ottoman and Pasha references naturally, then states the practical danger in Julio's cautious voice.

records.english: Pasha's waters can wait until later.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael summarizes Julio's advice in the route branch focused on Ottoman influence.
records.source_meaning: Raphael concludes that they should postpone visiting Mediterranean waters strongly influenced by the Ottoman Pasha's forces.
records.localization_note: Preserves Raphael's conclusion to postpone this region without adding a reason unstated in the source.

records.english: Then we should leave waters controlled by Valdes and the Pasha for later.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: In the broader route branch, Raphael summarizes the need to avoid both Spanish and Ottoman spheres of influence.
records.source_meaning: Raphael concludes that Mediterranean areas heavily influenced by Spain's Valdes fleet and the Ottoman Pasha's fleet should be left until later.
records.localization_note: Keeps both named threats in a natural strategic conclusion without adding a condition absent from the source.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}No need to force a contract. Best not to provoke them.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio advises against aggressive contracting in hostile faction territory.
records.source_meaning: Julio says they need not force a contract and should avoid carelessly provoking the hostile power.
records.localization_note: The concise advice is an idiomatic rendering of Julio's cautious strategy.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Large cities may have talented navigators. We should visit them and recruit allies.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio balances his warning with the need to recruit crew members in major cities.
records.source_meaning: Julio says large cities may hold excellent navigators, so they cannot be ignored and should be visited at least to seek companions.
records.localization_note: Recruit new allies naturally conveys looking for companions in gameplay terms without reducing them to resources.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}Good plan.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus approves Julio's balanced strategy.
records.source_meaning: Janus calls the plan wise.
records.localization_note: A wise plan supplies the implied subject naturally in English.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Right. We'll need better ships and more training for other seas.{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio recognizes that both the fleet and crew must improve before expanding outward.
records.source_meaning: Claudio says that to venture into other seas, they must strengthen their ships and train themselves as well.
records.localization_note: Keeps Claudio's direct voice and naturally contrasts stronger ships with better-trained sailors.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Exactly. Remember: visit large cities and recruit navigators.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio reinforces the recruitment objective before the group sets out.
records.source_meaning: Julio agrees and reminds Raphael to tour large cities and gather navigators.
records.localization_note: Keeps the reminder direct and avoids repeating Japanese connective phrasing.

records.english: Wow, we have so much to do!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael reacts to the growing list of strategic objectives.
records.source_meaning: Raphael exclaims that there are many things they need to do.
records.localization_note: Uses an enthusiastic complete sentence suited to Raphael.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}Things are getting busy.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus dryly observes that the voyage has become much busier.
records.source_meaning: Janus says things are about to become busy.
records.localization_note: The understated phrasing preserves Janus's composed voice.

records.english: Let's do our best!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael enthusiastically commits the group to the next stage of their voyage.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says they should do their best.
records.localization_note: Let's do this captures the energizing effect of the Japanese exhortation.

records.english: Athens is a city of learning and philosophy!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Upon arriving in Athens, Raphael recalls the city's intellectual reputation.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says Athens is known as a city of learning and philosophy.
records.localization_note: Removed the Japanese tag question so the compact line sounds enthusiastic rather than uncertain.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}This city makes you want to study.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus responds to Raphael's comment by describing Athens's scholarly atmosphere.
records.source_meaning: Janus says the atmosphere of the entire city makes him feel that he should study.
records.localization_note: Combined the repeated Japanese observation into one natural reflective sentence.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Why are you always so uptight?{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio teases the preceding speaker for responding to Athens with stiff seriousness.
records.source_meaning: Claudio asks whether the other person's rigid, overly formal personality can be changed.
records.localization_note: Uptight conveys Claudio's rough complaint without the unnatural literal image of stiffness.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Yeah, yeah. Got it. Enough from me.{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: After being scolded for complaining, Claudio sarcastically agrees to be quiet.
records.source_meaning: Claudio dismissively says he understands and will keep quiet.
records.localization_note: Yeah, yeah and Enough from me preserve his deliberately coarse, sarcastic agreement to be quiet.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Perfect timing. Time to investigate the Proof of Conquest.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: In scholarly Athens, Julio decides to investigate the legendary Proof of Conquest.
records.source_meaning: Julio says the timing is convenient and that he will investigate the Proof of Conquest.
records.localization_note: This is our chance makes the convenient timing conversational while preserving the named quest object.

records.english: Right... Why are you here, Julio?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael remembers that Julio had a particular reason for visiting Athens.
records.source_meaning: Raphael asks Julio what business brought him here.
records.localization_note: The direct question naturally asks what business brought Julio to Athens in this immediate context.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Time to investigate the Proof.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio answers Raphael by repeating the purpose of his visit to Athens.
records.source_meaning: Julio says he is going to investigate the Proof of Conquest.
records.localization_note: The direct answer retains Julio's matter-of-fact tone.

records.english: What's this Proof?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks Julio to explain the unfamiliar legendary object.
records.source_meaning: Raphael asks what the Proof of Conquest is.
records.localization_note: The contraction makes the straightforward question sound natural.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}That's the question.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains that learning what the Proof is forms the purpose of his investigation.
records.source_meaning: Julio says that is what he is going to investigate.
records.localization_note: Localized the repeated Japanese pronoun into a natural response to Raphael's question.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Wait here. This won't take long.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio leaves the group briefly to conduct his inquiry in Athens.
records.source_meaning: Julio tells them to wait and says he will return soon.
records.localization_note: Be right back is the natural American equivalent of returning immediately.

records.english: Huh...{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael is left puzzled after Julio walks away.
records.source_meaning: Raphael gives a puzzled, deflated sigh.
records.localization_note: Huh conveys confusion more naturally here than a literal sigh syllable.

records.english: Hm? What's that?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael notices a nearby dispute involving an elderly traveler.
records.source_meaning: Raphael notices something and wonders what it is.
records.localization_note: The compact reaction preserves the shift of attention.

records.english: Excuse me. What's wrong?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael approaches Hans after overhearing a sailor refuse him passage.
records.source_meaning: Raphael politely asks whether something is wrong.
records.localization_note: Excuse me supplies the natural polite opening implied by the hesitant Japanese address.

records.english: You want to sail... Should we bring you along?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael considers whether to grant Hans passage after hearing his request.
records.source_meaning: Raphael understands that Hans wants to voyage and wonders what decision to make.
records.localization_note: Sail captures the desired voyage without implying a specific destination.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Why take on another old man?{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio objects to recruiting Hans, joking that the crew already has enough elderly men.
records.source_meaning: Claudio asks what good it would do to keep bringing old men aboard.
records.localization_note: Another preserves the source's plural complaint in compact, idiomatic English.

records.english: Tell us why you want to go. Then we'll decide.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Rather than refuse Hans outright, Raphael asks him to explain his purpose.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says they should hear Hans's reason first and make a judgment afterward.
records.localization_note: Uses a clear two-step response that reflects Raphael's fair-minded leadership.

records.english: Hmm...{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael considers Hans's desire to study the whole world.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says he understands.
records.localization_note: The reflective pause is retained without a manual line break.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Admirable!{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio is suddenly moved by Hans's commitment to research.
records.source_meaning: Claudio exclaims that Hans is admirable.
records.localization_note: Admirable directly conveys Claudio's abrupt praise within the tight allocation.

records.english: Claudio?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael is surprised by Claudio's sudden admiration for Hans.
records.source_meaning: Raphael addresses Claudio in surprise.
records.localization_note: Uses Claudio's full localized name rather than the Japanese nickname Clau.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}At his age, he's braving dangerous seas for his research. Now that's dedication! He has my respect!{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio passionately explains why Hans's dangerous scholarly voyage has won his respect.
records.source_meaning: Claudio praises Hans for pushing his aging body onto dangerous seas solely to complete his research and says he respects that spirit.
records.localization_note: Now that's spirit captures Claudio's emphatic admiration without mimicking the Japanese clause order.

records.english: Y-yeah, you're right. Hans, join us.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Prompted by Claudio's passion, Raphael invites Hans to join the crew.
records.source_meaning: Raphael hesitantly agrees with Claudio, then politely tells Hans he may board.
records.localization_note: Join us is a concise invitation that preserves Raphael's decision.

records.english: What is it?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael asks Hans to state the additional favor he has mentioned.
records.source_meaning: Raphael asks what Hans wants.
records.localization_note: The direct question remains polite in the established conversational context.

records.english: {SPEAKER:08}Arcadius Eudoxios. Glad to meet you.{PAD}
records.speaker: Arcadius Eudoxios
records.context: Hans's assistant formally introduces himself to Raphael's crew.
records.source_meaning: Arcadius states his full name and politely asks for their goodwill.
records.localization_note: The conventional polite introduction suits Arcadius's reserved, formal voice.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}(Wow... He's awfully slender.){PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus privately reacts to Arcadius's delicate build.
records.source_meaning: Janus thinks that Arcadius is very slender and delicate-looking.
records.localization_note: Awfully slender keeps the surprised observation without making a stronger claim about health or gender.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}(You're one to talk. Still, he does make Janus look sturdy.){PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio silently mocks Janus for commenting on Arcadius's build, then concedes the comparison.
records.source_meaning: Claudio thinks Janus has no room to criticize, though Arcadius does make Janus appear robust by comparison.
records.localization_note: You're one to talk is the idiomatic retort; the comparison is retained without the authored Japanese indentation.

records.english: Ahem!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael clears his throat, interrupting the private appraisal of Arcadius.
records.source_meaning: Raphael clears his throat emphatically.
records.localization_note: Ahem is the standard English sound for the source action.

records.english: {SPEAKER:08}Navigation is among my studies, but there's still much all of you can teach me.{PAD}
records.speaker: Arcadius Eudoxios
records.context: Arcadius modestly describes his limited navigation training to the crew.
records.source_meaning: Arcadius says he has studied navigation a little but expects everyone aboard to teach him many things.
records.localization_note: Much to learn conveys his formal humility without repetitive Japanese qualifiers.

records.english: Don't worry about it. We're only getting started ourselves.{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael reassures Arcadius that the existing crew members are novices too.
records.source_meaning: Raphael tells Arcadius not to overthink it because they themselves are only just beginning.
records.localization_note: Don't worry about it is warmer and more conversational than a literal instruction not to think too seriously.

records.english: {SPEAKER:08}That's reassuring.{PAD}
records.speaker: Arcadius Eudoxios
records.context: Arcadius relaxes after Raphael's reassurance.
records.source_meaning: Arcadius says hearing that puts him at ease.
records.localization_note: The concise response preserves Arcadius's reserved politeness.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}This voyage should be fun.{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus looks forward to the voyage after Hans and Arcadius join.
records.source_meaning: Janus says the voyage seems likely to be enjoyable.
records.localization_note: Enjoyable fits Janus's composed register better than the more casual fun.

records.english: A scholar aboard will help us. Right, Claudio?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael welcomes Hans's expertise and seeks Claudio's agreement.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says traveling with a broadly learned scholar is reassuring and asks Claudio to agree.
records.localization_note: Aboard supplies the natural nautical context, and Claudio replaces the source nickname.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Yeah, guess so. Keep up the good work, Doctor! You too, Assistant!{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio awkwardly encourages Hans and Arcadius after accepting their value to the crew.
records.source_meaning: Claudio agrees, tells the doctor to study hard, and then adds the assistant emphatically.
records.localization_note: Yeah, guess so preserves his gruff reluctance; capitalized forms are direct joking addresses, not invented ranks.

records.english: {SPEAKER:08}Pleased to join you...{PAD}
records.speaker: Arcadius Eudoxios
records.context: Arcadius responds politely to Claudio's rough welcome.
records.source_meaning: Arcadius politely asks for everyone's continued goodwill.
records.localization_note: The standard collaborative phrase suits his formal reserve and preserves the trailing hesitation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Hey!{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio calls out when he spots Raphael's group with Hans.
records.source_meaning: Julio calls loudly to the group.
records.localization_note: Hey is the natural compact attention-getter.

records.english: Oh, Julio!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael recognizes Julio returning from his investigation.
records.source_meaning: Raphael notices Julio and addresses him.
records.localization_note: The exclamation naturally reflects recognition.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Hm? So this is where you've been!{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio realizes he has found the person he was seeking alongside Raphael.
records.source_meaning: Julio notices the person and exclaims that this is where he has been.
records.localization_note: The sentence preserves Julio's surprised recognition without overexplaining the referent.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Hans! There you are!{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio reveals that Hans is the old acquaintance he came to find.
records.source_meaning: Julio calls Hans by name and says he searched for him.
records.localization_note: The present-perfect form sounds natural upon finally finding someone.

records.english: What?! You were looking for him?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael realizes that Julio's investigation and Hans's recruitment have unexpectedly converged.
records.source_meaning: Raphael reacts in surprise and asks whether Julio was searching for Hans.
records.localization_note: He was the one naturally emphasizes the coincidence.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Yes. He's an acquaintance who's studied the Proof for years.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio explains his relationship with Hans and Hans's relevance to the quest.
records.source_meaning: Julio says Hans is an acquaintance who has researched the Proof of Conquest for many years.
records.localization_note: Old acquaintance refers to a long-standing connection and does not invent intimacy.

records.english: Not really... What exactly is this Proof of Conquest?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael corrects Hans's assumption that the crew already knows about the Proof.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says they cannot be interested in something they know nothing about and asks what the Proof of Conquest is.
records.localization_note: Not really naturally answers Hans's question while leading into Raphael's request for an explanation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:08}Treasures lie across the seas, destined for each sea's ruler.{PAD}
records.speaker: Arcadius Eudoxios
records.context: Arcadius gives Raphael the first concise explanation of the Proofs of Conquest.
records.source_meaning: Arcadius says they are treasures scattered among different seas and are literally said to come into the hands of those who rule each sea.
records.localization_note: Uses plural pronouns because the following explanation establishes seven separate treasures.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}You figured it out?{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio asks whether Hans's research has uncovered a lead to the Proofs.
records.source_meaning: Julio asks whether Hans has figured it out.
records.localization_note: A clue follows Hans's statement about finding a lead and avoids overstating that the mystery is solved.

records.english: Then we can collect them ourselves!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael realizes the crew could pursue all seven maps described by Hans.
records.source_meaning: Raphael suggests that they could collect them with their own hands.
records.localization_note: Ourselves conveys personal agency without the awkward literal reference to their hands.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Exactly. Then you'd truly be ruler of the world's seas.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio confirms the magnitude of Raphael's newly imagined quest.
records.source_meaning: Julio says that doing so would make Raphael the genuine ruler of the seas in both name and reality.
records.localization_note: Truly compresses the paired Japanese idioms about authenticity and reputation.

records.english: Let's do it! We'll claim them!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael commits himself and the crew to earning the Proofs of Conquest.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says they should do it and win the Proofs through their own power.
records.localization_note: Win them preserves the sense of earning rather than merely finding the treasures.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}As usual, {MACRO:FI}'s first in line. Hard to follow, but we need to see a Proof first.{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio comments on Raphael's enthusiasm and agrees that seeing a Proof is the first practical step.
records.source_meaning: Claudio says FI is always the most eager; although he does not fully understand, nothing can begin until they see the thing called a Proof.
records.localization_note: The clipped Don't get it matches Claudio's casual voice, and the protagonist macro is preserved exactly.

records.english: Yeah! We'll find one!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael confidently responds to Claudio's practical challenge.
records.source_meaning: Raphael declares that he will definitely find it.
records.localization_note: Uses inclusive we'll because this is now the crew's shared quest.

records.english: All right! We'll find one and someday challenge Hayreddin too!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael connects the new quest with his longer-term ambition to challenge Hayreddin.
records.source_meaning: Raphael vows to find the Proof and someday challenge Hayreddin as well.
records.localization_note: Uses them for the established multiple Proofs while keeping the singular personal challenge.

records.english: {SPEAKER:08}Hayreddin?!{PAD}
records.speaker: Arcadius Eudoxios
records.context: Arcadius is shocked by Raphael's ambition to challenge the legendary Hayreddin.
records.source_meaning: Arcadius repeats Hayreddin's name in surprise.
records.localization_note: The source reaction is already natural and retains the established spelling.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Ho ho! A bit late to notice. Our admiral fears nothing!{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio laughs at Hans and Arcadius's surprise and praises Raphael's fearlessness.
records.source_meaning: Julio laughs, says it is too late to realize this now, and calls the admiral someone who knows no fear.
records.localization_note: Fearless provides a natural positive summation of the Japanese idiom.

records.english: Really?{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael reacts to the rumor that a Proof map was taken toward southern Africa.
records.source_meaning: Raphael asks whether the rumor is true.
records.localization_note: The compact question retains his surprised interest within the tight allocation.

records.english: Understood. Let's head for Africa!{PAD}
records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael chooses southern Africa as the crew's next lead in the search for a Proof map.
records.source_meaning: Raphael acknowledges the uncertain lead and says they should go to Africa.
records.localization_note: Combined the Japanese acknowledgments into one decisive transition.

records.english: {SPEAKER:71}What?! No ship would agree to that! Try elsewhere!{PAD}
records.speaker: Athens port worker
records.context: A port worker rejects Hans's request for free passage to a distant country.
records.source_meaning: The worker reacts in disbelief, says no ship that convenient exists, and tells Hans to ask elsewhere.
records.localization_note: Makes the implied request for passage explicit while retaining the brusque refusal.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Deck, hold, anywhere is fine. Just take me far away.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans insists he will accept any accommodation if a ship carries him abroad.
records.source_meaning: Hans says the deck or hold is fine and asks only to be taken to a distant country.
records.localization_note: Some distant land sounds more natural than an unspecified distant country in this plea.

records.english: {SPEAKER:71}At your age, you couldn't even swab the deck!{PAD}
records.speaker: Athens port worker
records.context: The port worker dismisses Hans as too old to earn passage through shipboard labor.
records.source_meaning: The worker says that at Hans's age, even cleaning the deck would be impossible.
records.localization_note: Scrub the deck is the natural nautical phrasing for the cited work.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Please, reconsider.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans makes one last gentle appeal to the port worker.
records.source_meaning: Hans asks the worker not to say that and pleads with him again.
records.localization_note: Reconsider naturally expresses the repeated request without copying the Japanese tag appeal.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}You're sailors, aren't you? Please let me aboard!{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans notices Raphael's newly arrived crew and asks them for passage.
records.source_meaning: Hans recognizes them as sailors entering port and asks to board their ship.
records.localization_note: Would you let me aboard is polite and appropriately hopeful.

records.english: {SPEAKER:71}Don't do it, Captain. This old man expects a free ride!{PAD}
records.speaker: Athens port worker
records.context: The port worker warns Raphael that Hans cannot pay or work for his passage.
records.source_meaning: The worker advises the captain against it and says Hans wants to be taken aboard for free.
records.localization_note: Free ride is the natural idiom and does not imply deceit beyond the worker's complaint.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}So... you refuse?{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans dejectedly assumes Raphael will refuse after Claudio objects.
records.source_meaning: Hans asks whether the answer is indeed no.
records.localization_note: States the implied refusal in natural English without adding a reason.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}My name is Hans Retzel, naturalist.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans introduces himself after Raphael asks why he wants to sail.
records.source_meaning: Hans gives his name and says he is a scholar who researches natural history.
records.localization_note: Naturalist is the concise, accurate profession; the full introduction avoids a broken English fragment.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}The whole world is my subject! Please, let me see it!{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans passionately explains that travel is essential to his worldwide research.
records.source_meaning: Hans says everything in the world is a subject for his research and begs Raphael to show him the world.
records.localization_note: Field of study preserves both his scholarly purpose and the global scope of his plea.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}You mean it? Thank you!{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans gratefully confirms that Raphael is truly offering him passage.
records.source_meaning: Hans asks whether Raphael really permits it and expresses gratitude.
records.localization_note: You mean it is the natural excited confirmation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Admiral, one more favor, if you please...{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: After receiving passage, Hans hesitantly asks Raphael for an additional accommodation.
records.source_meaning: Hans addresses the admiral and says that, since he is already being selfish, he has one more request.
records.localization_note: If you please conveys his apologetic awareness that he is asking an additional favor.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}May one companion come along?{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans reveals that he wants passage for his assistant as well.
records.source_meaning: Hans hesitantly asks Raphael to let one traveling companion board.
records.localization_note: One companion preserves the count without prematurely identifying Arcadius.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}My assistant, a promising young... man. Ahem. Arcadius, introduce yourself.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans presents Arcadius, awkwardly hesitating over his description before prompting an introduction.
records.source_meaning: Hans says Arcadius is his assistant and a promising young man, hesitates and clears his throat, then asks Arcadius to greet everyone.
records.localization_note: Preserves the conspicuous hesitation without explaining or resolving its intended joke.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}He's a devoted and promising young... man.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans resumes praising Arcadius after the crew's private comments, again hesitating over young man.
records.source_meaning: Hans says Arcadius has not only a strong attitude toward scholarship but considerable promise as a young man.
records.localization_note: The repeated hesitation is retained because it is deliberate characterization, not a layout pause.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Wonderful! All is well. Our grand voyage begins!{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: With both Hans and Arcadius accepted, Hans celebrates the beginning of the voyage.
records.source_meaning: Hans exclaims that everything is going well and that a wonderful voyage is beginning.
records.localization_note: All is well conveys the favorable convergence without implying supernatural luck.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Leave it to me!{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans enthusiastically accepts Claudio's charge to continue his research.
records.source_meaning: Hans tells Claudio to entrust the research to him.
records.localization_note: Leave it to me is the idiomatic confident response.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Julio! What a surprise!{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans recognizes his old acquaintance Julio with delighted surprise.
records.source_meaning: Hans exclaims that the man is Julio.
records.localization_note: What a surprise naturally conveys Hans's delighted recognition without overstating disbelief.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Oh! The Proof interests you too?{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans assumes Raphael's crew shares Julio's interest in the legendary Proof.
records.source_meaning: Hans asks whether Raphael and the others are also interested in the Proof of Conquest.
records.localization_note: The plural you naturally addresses the crew without awkward expansion.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Much remains a mystery, but a clue may point us toward the treasures.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans explains that his research may finally point toward the Proofs' locations.
records.source_meaning: Hans says the details remain mysterious, but it appears they may find a lead that can locate the treasures.
records.localization_note: The treasures refers to the multiple Proofs established by Arcadius and keeps Hans's uncertainty.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Ancient texts name seven treasures. The Seven Sages marked each sealing place on maps of many shapes.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans summarizes the ancient textual evidence behind the seven Proof maps.
records.source_meaning: Hans says old documents describe seven treasures and that the Seven Sages marked the places where they should be sealed on maps of various forms.
records.localization_note: Ancient texts and Seven Sages follow established quest terminology while removing Japanese passive stacking.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Someday, each sea's ruler is destined to receive its map.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans explains the prophecy linking each map to the future ruler of its sea.
records.source_meaning: Hans says that one day the person who rules each sea is fated to obtain that sea's map.
records.localization_note: Makes the one-map-per-sea relationship explicit without inventing how destiny chooses the recipient.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Good heavens! What a crew!{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans reacts to Raphael's ambition and wonders at the crew he has just joined.
records.source_meaning: Hans says he is astonished and may have boarded an incredible ship.
records.localization_note: Good heavens fits his age and scholarly register without caricaturing him.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Ah, youth is a wonderful thing.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans warmly reflects on Raphael's fearless youthful ambition.
records.source_meaning: Hans murmurs agreement and says being young is a good thing.
records.localization_note: Ah preserves his thoughtful murmur without copying the repeated Japanese sound.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Rumor says someone took a Proof map to the seas south of Africa.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans offers the crew its first geographical lead toward a Proof map.
records.source_meaning: Hans says he recently heard that someone took one map of the Proof of Conquest to the south of Africa.
records.localization_note: Seas south of Africa preserves the uncertain destination without naming a specific ocean.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}The rumor may be false, but Africa could yield a clue.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans cautions Raphael that the African lead is unverified but worth pursuing.
records.source_meaning: Hans does not know whether the rumor is true, but thinks going to Africa may reveal something.
records.localization_note: Can't vouch for naturally communicates uncertainty about the rumor's truth.

records.english: {SPEAKER:4B}Shipboard work is beyond me, but call me with any item questions.{PAD}
records.speaker: Hans Retzel
records.context: Hans explains his advisory role after joining Raphael's crew.
records.source_meaning: Hans says he cannot perform shipboard work but asks for their goodwill and tells them to call him with item questions.
records.localization_note: Call me with any questions clearly conveys his advisory role without suggesting technical shipboard duties.
